title: 1969 AHSME Problem 16
statement: When \((a-b)^n,\) \(n\ge2,\) \(ab\ne0,\) is expanded by the binomial theorem, it is found that, when \(a=kb,\) where \(k\) is a positive integer, the sum of the second and third terms is zero. Then \(n\) equals:

solutions.text:
The sum of the second and third terms is \[ -na^{n-1}b+\frac{n(n-1)}2a^{n-2}b^2. \] Substituting \(a=kb\) and dividing by the nonzero quantity \(na^{n-2}b\) gives \[ -k+\frac{n-1}{2}=0. \] Therefore \(n=2k+1.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: The second and third terms are \(-na^{n-1}b\) and \(\binom n2a^{n-2}b^2\)
